name: Matthew Leitao
title: Behavioral Scientist and Quantitative Researcher
summary: Behavioral scientist with 13+ years of research experience and a PhD from Georgetown. Designs and analyzes randomized experiments, surveys and longitudinal studies on how people trust and use AI. Analyzes student-outcome data for universities, with dashboards used by administrators.

experience.org: National Human Genome Research Institute, National Institutes of Health
experience.role: Postdoctoral Researcher (IRTA), Social and Behavioral Research Branch
bullets: Managed six research projects, including a ghrelin-related pharmacology randomized controlled trial under FDA oversight.
Analyzed data from the trial's virtual reality buffet simulation and first-authored the paper in the Journal of Medical Extended Reality.
Led the design of a 2 x 3 vignette experiment on how a standard result, a geneticist's review or an AI review changes trust in a genetic risk result.
Taught Introduction to R and Introduction to Quarto to colleagues.
Designed and ran six preregistered studies on trust in medical AI, including a 15-day daily-diary study with random assignment to AI or doctor advice.
Co-led generative AI experiments on how people collaborate with AI at work, with business-school collaborators; the paper is under review.
Managed five research assistants across six or seven concurrent projects.
Taught Psychology of Technology as instructor of record and received the 2023 Graduate Student Teaching Award.
Coordinated the department research pool, where participant yield rose 50% over the prior year.

experience.org: Georgetown University, Office of Assessment and Decision Support
bullets: Analyzed class size and instructor time by student rank, faculty type, ethnicity and gender, and presented initial findings.
Used multilevel modeling to evaluate longitudinal student outcomes and trajectories.
Built the evidence on how useful the GRE was in recruitment and interviews, and presented it to faculty and administrators. The program then made the GRE optional.

experience.org: California State University, Northridge, Office of Institutional Research
bullets: Merged, cleaned and analyzed campus-wide records on more than 100,000 students to learn how student choices relate to academic outcomes.
Compared how first-year unit load relates to GPA, retention and graduation for athletes, Pell-eligible students and students served by disability services.
Built Tableau dashboards that administrators, chairs and deans used, and presented the findings to university administration.

experience.org: California State University, Northridge, Applied Social Psychology Lab
bullets: Coordinated the lab and trained 14 lab assistants.
Wrote and defended a preregistered thesis on obedience to computer authority.

experience.org: University of California, Riverside, OBSERVE Lab
bullets: Managed the schedules and reviews of 15 research assistants.
Wrote Excel macros and Praat scripts to process speech data.

publications: Leitao, M. R., Farokhnia, M., Leggio, L., & Persky, S. (2026). Experiences and behavior during a virtual reality buffet simulation: A secondary analysis of a ghrelin-related pharmacology randomized controlled trial. Journal of Medical Extended Reality.
Leitao, M. R., Proulx, J. D. E., & Kushlev, K. (2024). Smartphones undermine social connectedness more in men than women: A mini mega-analysis. Technology, Mind, and Behavior, 5(1).
Logg, J. M.†, Leitao, M. R.†, & Ulu, C. The cost of generative AI collaboration strategies to the psychological experience of work. Under review. † Co-first authors.

Tableau, Qualtrics, Prolific, CloudResearch, Mechanical Turk, SONA, Quarto, Excel
Randomized experiments, survey design, daily-diary studies, multilevel and longitudinal modeling, causal inference, mixed methods, preregistration
